item.title: Ninja-dera (Myoryuji Temple): A Temple Full of Hidden Defensive Traps — Guide
item.description: Myoryuji Temple, nicknamed Ninja-dera or ‘Ninja Temple’ despite having no actual historical connection to ninjas, was built in the mid-17th century by the Maeda clan as a disguised defensive lookout post, its unassuming temple exterior concealing an interior riddled with hidden staircases, trapdoors, secret rooms and a lookout tower designed to detect approaching threats. The nickname comes from these deceptive architectural tricks rather than any ninja history, and the temple can only be visited on a guided tour, which must be booked in advance by phone or online.
